You should be careful so that not to mix personal and business expenses.

history.text: Find a bank offering a free checking account, especially if you don't anticipate much activity. Other accounts, such as IRAs and discount brokerage, are also free. If you think it would be beneficial to open another account, feel free to do so.

history.speaker: agent
history.text: There are advantages and disadvantages to keeping all your accounts with the same bank versus having accounts at different banks. history.speaker: user
history.text: Is it worth having a web chat widget on my website?

history.speaker: agent
history.text: Yes, it is worth having a web chat widget on your website. The web chat integration can help your customers with common questions and tasks; it can understand customer messages in any of the languages that are supported by the service, and it engages your users when they need help, answering their questions quickly and efficiently, and providing fallback options so there is always a path to a solution. It is also customizable, secure, and supports a wide range of desktop and mobile browsers. Building a custom user interface for these functionalities would require significant time and effort, which could be better spent on building a high-quality assistant. Additionally, the web chat widget is easy for you to deploy and easy for customers to use.

history.speaker: user
history.text: how to add web chat widget?

history.speaker: agent
history.text: From the Assistants page, click to open the assistant tile that you want to deploy to your site. From the Integrations section, click the Web chat tile and click Open. The Open web chat window opens. In the Environment field, select the environment you want the web chat widget to connect to. Click Confirm. All you need to do is embed a generated script element in your HTML source.

history.speaker: user
history.text: Can I extend the web chat? if so, how can I do that?

history.speaker: agent
history.text: Yes, extend the web chat. If you are a developer, you can extend the capabilities of the web chat by using the Watson Assistant web chat toolkit on GitHub. You can also you can further customize and extend the web chat by writing code and using the web chat API.

history.speaker: user
history.text: Is web chat secure enough for me to pass some sesitive data?

history.speaker: agent
history.text: When you enable web chat security, all messages received by the web chat integration that are not accompanied by a properly signed JSON Web Token (JWT) will be rejected. JWTs are digitally signed using a private encryption key that only you have, ensuring that each message originates with your website. You can also use the public key provided by IBM to add an additional level of encryption for passing sensitive data from the web chat. This private context variable will be available for use by the dialog but not by anything else.

history.speaker: user
history.text: I do not like the look of my web chat and how it opens and closes...

history.speaker: agent
history.text: You can customize the look and behavior of your web chat. From the Style tab of the web chat configuration page, you can change the color of the launcher icon and the text font. You can choose to use a different base Carbon Design theme as well. If you want to make more advanced customizations, you can change the launcher icon used to open the web chat widget and how it opens and closes. For example, you can launch the web chat from a different button or process on your website, open it in a different location or size, hide the launcher icon entirely, or hide the close button.

history.text: Are the Lite pricing plans available with all account types in IBM Cloud

history.speaker: agent
history.text: Yes, Lite pricing plans are available with all account types in IBM Cloud. You can have one instance of a Lite plan for each service. For more information about Lite accounts, you can refer to the Account types documentation.

history.text: What is it?

history.text: The Lite plan is a free service plan with usage quotas. You can use the Lite plan to develop an app without any charges. The plan may be renewed monthly or used as a one-time offer. Lite pricing plans are accessible for all account types, and you can have one instance of a Lite plan for each service.

history.speaker: user
history.text: What is an account?

history.speaker: agent
history.text: Your IBM Cloud account consists of various interconnected components and systems for managing resources, users, and access. Understanding how these components are linked and how access functions will help you set up your account effectively. An IBM Cloud account is necessary for provisioning and managing IBM Cloud services that are part of the IBM Cloud for Financial Services reference architectures. In addition to outlining the high-level steps to follow, we will also describe some best practices for setting up your account that will assist you in meeting the requirements of the IBM Cloud Framework for Financial Services. We will also provide the most relevant control requirements.

history.speaker: user
history.text: How can I create one?

history.speaker: agent
history.text:
To sign up for an IBM Cloud account, you can use an existing IBMid or create a new one. Simply go to the IBM Cloud login page and click on "Create an IBM Cloud account." Then, enter your IBMid email address. If you don't have an existing IBMid, an ID will be created based on the email you enter. Complete the remaining fields with your information.
You will be prompted to provide your credit card information to verify your identity and secure your account. It's important to note that you can try out IBM Cloud for free and only pay for the billable services that you choose to use, with no long-term contracts or commitments. After filling out the information, click "Create account" and then confirm your account by clicking the link in the confirmation email sent to your provided email address.
Finally, you can see the "Account types" section to compare and choose an account type that suits your needs.

history.speaker: user
history.text: How many megabytes can I use each month?

history.speaker: agent
history.text: If you signed up for a Lite account before 12 August 2021, you can use a limited number of free buildpacks and Cloud Foundry apps with up to 256 MB of free instantaneous runtime memory per month. If you created a Lite account before 25 October 2021, your account doesn't expire, and you can access IBM Cloud services for free with select Lite plans, which are marked with a Lite tag in the catalog. To access all Free plans, you can upgrade to a Pay-As-You-Go account by adding your credit card information.
